title: The merry men
summary: The Merry Men is a collection of four stories by Robert Louis Stevenson, published in a 1904 edition, with a Project Gutenberg text. The title piece is a novella-length tale narrated by a young Edinburgh student who returns to his uncle's remote Scottish island of Aros, where wrecks, the dangerous tidal Roost, and a legend of a sunken Spanish treasure ship shape a growing sense of dread. Other pieces include "Will o' the Mill," a reflective tale of a miller's life, "Markheim," a psychological story of a murderer confronting his conscience, "Thrawn Janet," a Scots tale of a minister haunted by a sinister housekeeper, "Olalla," a Gothic story set in a decayed Spanish household, and "The Treasure of Franchard," a comic sequence about a dying mountebank's hidden fortune and a philosophical young man's misadventures. The stories mix supernatural horror, moral reckoning, and wry humour, and show Stevenson's range across Scottish, Spanish and French settings.
